vopros: What's the best AI receptionist for a small business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
There's no single universal "best" AI receptionist — the right pick depends heavily on your industry, call volume, and budget. That said, a few names come up consistently across independent comparisons (note: many "best AI receptionist" articles are published by the vendors themselves, so take #1 rankings with a grain of salt). Here's an honest breakdown:

## Top picks by use case

**Best for home services / contractors (plumbers, HVAC, electricians):**
Rosie is aimed squarely at small service businesses, and it's the one most contractors and home-services owners get running fastest — you point it at your website and Google Business Profile and it trains itself on what your business does. One firm that tested it across portfolio companies found Rosie was the best fit for most of their portfolio companies, from a single-location plumber to a 50+ location oil change franchise.

**Best if you want optional human backup:**
Smith.ai is the better fit when optional human involvement is required, while Ruby is the live receptionist choice for teams that want every call answered by a person. Keep in mind human backup is often priced as a per-call add-on ($3 per handoff at Smith.ai, for example), not included in base plans.

**Best if you want a fully human option:**
Ruby is a live virtual receptionist service with 200+ reviews on G2 and a 4.7/5.0 rating — real humans answer your calls, not AI. If you prioritize the warmth and flexibility of human conversation and are willing to pay a premium, Ruby delivers the highest quality human phone experience.

**Best if you already use RingCentral:**
RingCentral's AI Receptionist works with any existing phone system — you don't need to switch providers or port numbers; the AI layers on top of what you already have, with multilingual support in 7 languages and CRM integrations with Salesforce and HubSpot.

**Best budget/entry-level option:**
Dialzara offers the lowest entry point for AI receptionist service at $29/month for 60 minutes — a good option for solopreneurs and very small businesses that receive fewer than 30 calls per month.

**Best for appointment-heavy businesses (salons, spas, clinics):**
Frontdesk-style tools are built specifically for booking-focused businesses where the phone is essentially a scheduling line.

## What to actually watch out for

1. **Pricing models vary wildly.** Per-minute pricing (Ruby, PATLive, Abby Connect) makes costs unpredictable and can cost $300-$1,000+/month for moderate call volumes, while flat-rate plans avoid that risk.
2. **Per-minute rounding is a hidden cost.** Most per-minute plans round every call up to the next 60 seconds — even rounding to 6-second increments adds ~6.7% to your effective rate; a 20-second "are you open today?" bills as a full minute.
3. **Test before you commit.** Always use the free trial before committing — call the AI yourself 10+ times with realistic scenarios to evaluate voice quality, comprehension, and accuracy.
4. **Industry-specific training matters** — providers with home-services or medical-specific training tend to outperform generic solutions in their verticals.

## My honest recommendation

For most small businesses just getting started: **try Rosie or Dialzara first** (both cheap, fast setup, strong reputation among independent reviewers) to see if a pure-AI solution meets your needs. If your calls are high-stakes or emotionally sensitive (law firm intake, medical, high-end services), lean toward **Smith.ai** (AI + human hybrid) or **Ruby** (fully human) instead.

Given how saturated this market is with vendor-written "best of" lists, I'd suggest running trials with 2-3 candidates on your actual phone scripts rather than trusting any single ranking — including this one.
